neutral_facts.value: The accused and co-accused were seen with the victim on a specific date. The victim was later found dead in a canal. The body was recovered several days later, and a post-mortem was conducted. The medical report indicated the victim had sustained grievous injuries. Evidence included recovered items such as the victim's chappal, blood-stained clothing of the accused, and a blade with blood traces. The prosecution alleged that the accused and co-accused conspired to kill the victim at the instance of the victim's wife. The accused and co-accused were convicted of murder and other charges. The courts below found the circumstantial evidence complete and the accused had the opportunity to commit the crime.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the accused and co-accused killed the deceased at the instance of deceased's wife and threw away the body in the canal. There was a conspiracy among the accused, co-accused, and the deceased's wife to do away with the deceased. The accused and co-accused were convicted under sections 302, 1208, and 201 IPC and sentenced accordingly by the courts below.

quotes.text: The prosecution argued that the accused and co-accused killed the deceased at the instance of deceased's wife and threw away the body in the canal.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that there could be no motive for the appellant to commit the offence. They contended that the courts below committed an error in applying the last seen theory due to the long gap between the last seen and the recovery of the dead body. They also claimed that the recovery of incriminating material was not proved in accordance with law and that no independent witness had been examined.

quotes.text: There could be no motive for committing the offence so far as the appellant is concerned.
The courts below committed an error in applying the last seen theory.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that the last seen theory comes into play only in a case where the time gap between the point of time when the accused and the deceased were seen alive and when the deceased was found dead is small. The court also considered the credibility of witness statements and the admissibility of evidence despite minor discrepancies.

quotes.text: Last seen theory comes into play only in a case where the time gap is small between the point of time when the accused and the deceased were seen alive and when the deceased was found dead.
